response:
## The problem

Several of our feature branches have been open for three to six weeks. By the time they merge, they've drifted so far from main that integration itself becomes a multi-day project, often revealing conflicts nobody anticipated. Bugs surface only after merge, once the code is far from the context in which it was written, and a review of a 2,000-line branch is theater, not real scrutiny. We are twelve engineers effectively working in twelve slowly diverging copies of the codebase.

## The proposal

I'm proposing we move to trunk-based development: everyone commits small, incremental changes directly to main, or through branches that live under a day, with anything incomplete hidden behind a feature flag rather than isolated on a branch.

- Cut branch lifetime from weeks to under 24 hours, merging small diffs continuously.
- Wrap unfinished work in feature flags instead of long-lived branches.
- Require CI to pass and a lightweight review before every merge to main.
- Run a two-week pilot with one squad before rolling this out to all twelve of us.
- Track weekly merge-conflict time and defect-escape rate to judge the change.

## What could go wrong

The strongest objection is real, and I don't want to wave it away: without long branches, half-finished work sits on main, and a mistimed flag or a broken build could stall the whole team, not just one branch owner. Trunk-based development only works if our test suite is trustworthy and fast; today it is neither, and a flaky or slow pipeline would turn every commit into a gamble. That means this change only makes sense if we invest in test reliability and flag hygiene before we flip the switch, not after — and the pilot should be judged partly on whether we got that foundation right.

We should also expect a rough first couple of weeks as habits shift, and some real discomfort from engineers who value the privacy of an isolated branch. Both are manageable with training, pairing, and a clear rollback path if the pilot fails. Neither is a reason to keep a process that is visibly costing us more every sprint.

I would like a decision by the end of next week.
